items.stem: 46 students recorded the time, t minutes, they took to travel to school. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Time (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 5 | 5 < t ≤ 10 | 10 < t ≤ 15 | 15 < t ≤ 20 | 20 < t ≤ 25. Frequency: 8 | 9 | 9 | 8 | 12. Which is the modal class?
items.markingKey: Highest frequency is 12. [1]

items.stem: Explain why a mean worked out from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate.
items.answer: The exact data values are not known; each value is assumed to be at the midpoint of its class.
items.markingKey: B1 values unknown; B1 midpoint assumption. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the points of a frequency polygon are plotted at the midpoints of the classes.
items.answer: The values in each class are spread across the class, so the midpoint is used to represent all of them.
items.markingKey: B1 midpoint represents the class; B1 values unknown/spread. [2]

items.stem: An office in Muscat recorded the lengths, L minutes, of 33 phone calls. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Length (minutes): 0 < L ≤ 10 | 10 < L ≤ 20 | 20 < L ≤ 30 | 30 < L ≤ 40. Frequency: 11 | 3 | 12 | 7. Calculate an estimate of the mean length. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.answer: 19.5 minutes

items.stem: The distances, d metres, of 40 javelin throws were recorded at a competition in Mumbai. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Distance (m): 20 < d ≤ 25 | 25 < d ≤ 30 | 30 < d ≤ 35 | 35 < d ≤ 40. Frequency: 13 | 12 | 8 | 7. Calculate an estimate of the mean distance. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

36 students recorded the time, t minutes, they took to travel to school. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Time (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 5 | 5 < t ≤ 10 | 10 < t ≤ 15 | 15 < t ≤ 20 | 20 < t ≤ 25. Frequency: 3 | 6 | 4 | 8 | 15. (a) Write down the modal class. (b) Find the class that contains the median. (c) Explain why the mean can only be estimated from this table.
items.answer: (a) 20 < t ≤ 25 (b) 15 < t ≤ 20 (c) The exact values are not known; the midpoints are used to represent each class.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) M1 cumulative frequencies; A1 [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: A grouped frequency table has the class 240 < t ≤ 260. What is the midpoint of this class?

30 students recorded the time, t minutes, they took to travel to school. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Time (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 5 | 5 < t ≤ 10 | 10 < t ≤ 15 | 15 < t ≤ 20. Frequency: 3 | 4 | 12 | 11. Ines estimates the mean like this: Σ(upper class boundary × frequency) ÷ 30 = 455 ÷ 30 = 15.2. Explain Ines's mistake and work out a correct estimate of the mean, to 1 decimal place.
items.answer: Ines used the upper class boundaries instead of the midpoints. Correct estimate = 380 ÷ 30 = 12.7 minutes.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the error; M1 Σ(midpoint × f) ÷ total frequency; A1 value. [3]

items.stem: 42 students recorded the time, t minutes, they took to travel to school. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Explain Leila's mistake and work out a correct estimate of the mean, to 1 decimal place.
items.answer: Leila found the mean of the midpoints and ignored the frequencies. Correct estimate = 830 ÷ 42 = 19.8 minutes.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the error; M1 Σ(midpoint × f) ÷ total frequency; A1 value. [3]

items.stem: A museum in Hanoi records the number of visitors, in hundreds, each quarter. 2020: Q1 67, Q2 71, Q3 59, Q4 50; 2021: Q1 62, Q2 68, Q3 55, Q4 46. Work out the first 4-point moving average.

items.answer: The moving average represents all the values in that period, so it is plotted at the centre of the period.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the trend and the seasonal variation in a time series.
items.answer: The trend is the general long-term direction of the data; seasonal variation is a pattern that repeats in every cycle (for example each year).
items.markingKey: B1 trend; B1 seasonal. [2]

items.stem: A school in Bogotá records the electricity it uses, in hundreds of kWh, each quarter. 2020: Q1 41, Q2 42, Q3 34, Q4 45; 2021: Q1 45, Q2 45, Q3 38, Q4 50. items.stem: Explain why a strong correlation between two variables does not prove that one causes the other.
items.answer: Correlation only shows that the variables change together; a third factor could affect both, or the link could be coincidence.

items.stem: Explain the difference between interpolation and extrapolation when using a line of best fit.
items.answer: Interpolation estimates a value inside the range of the data and is usually reliable; extrapolation estimates outside the range and may be unreliable because the pattern may not continue.

items.answer: (a) the morning: 11.4 minutes; the afternoon: 9.7 minutes (b) the morning: 5 < t ≤ 10; the afternoon: 0 < t ≤ 5 (c) On average the values were greater in the morning (higher estimated mean).

items.stem: The 4-point moving averages for a set of quarterly data are 69.75, 69.5, 68, 67.25, 66.5, 65.5. Which statement best describes the trend?
options: The data have no seasonal variation
There is no clear upward or downward trend
items.answer: The trend is downward (decreasing)
items.markingKey: Look at how the moving averages change. [1]

items.stem: A school in Doha records the electricity it uses, in hundreds of kWh, each quarter. 2020: Q1 33, Q2 47, Q3 49, Q4 35; 2021: Q1 41, Q2 56, Q3 58, Q4 44. Chloe says: "The values fell from Q3 to Q4 of 2021, so the long-term trend is downward." Explain why Chloe is wrong.
items.answer: The fall from Q3 to Q4 also happened in 2020, so it is seasonal variation. Q4 2021 (44) is higher than Q4 2020 (35), and the 4-point moving averages rise from 41 to 49.75, so the trend is upward.
items.markingKey: B1 seasonal pattern; B1 evidence of upward trend (same-quarter comparison or moving averages). [2]

items.stem: A school records the number of students absent each week for 7 weeks. week 1: 88, week 2: 91, week 3: 92, week 4: 103, week 5: 106, week 6: 108, week 7: 104. Calculate the 3-point moving averages. Give your answers to 1 decimal place.
items.markingKey: M1 (88 + 91 + 92) ÷ 3; A1 all 5 correct.

items.stem: A sportswear shop in Manila records its sales, in thousands of dollars, each quarter. The 4-point moving averages are 40.75, 41.5, 42.5, 43.5, 44.5. Work out the mean change in the moving average per quarter, to 2 decimal places, and describe the trend.
items.answer: 0.94 per quarter; the trend is upward (increasing).

items.stem: A school in Karachi records the electricity it uses, in hundreds of kWh, each quarter. 2022: Q1 60, Q2 50, Q3 66, Q4 61; 2023: Q1 67, Q2 58, Q3 73, Q4 68. items.markingKey: (a) M1 first (60 + 50 + 66 + 61) ÷ 4; A2 all correct (A1 for 3 correct) [3] (b) B1 [1] (c) B1 quarter; B1 seasonal [2]

Two groups were compared using their test marks. Group A: median 70, range 40. Group B: median 56, range 30. Zara says group A is more consistent because its median is higher. Explain why Zara is wrong.
items.answer: Consistency is measured by the spread, not the average. Group B has the smaller range (30), so group B is more consistent.

items.stem: Here are the masses, in kg, of 15 suitcases checked in at Dubai airport: 25, 30, 20, 20, 19, 36, 14, 23, 19, 32, 12, 17, 35, 15, 24. (a) Draw an ordered stem-and-leaf diagram, with a key. items.stem: Data from Muscat show a strong positive correlation between the number of teachers in a city and the number of shops in the city. Omar says: "An increase in the number of teachers in a city causes an increase in the number of shops in the city." Explain why Omar may be wrong.
items.answer: Correlation does not prove causation. Both are probably affected by a third factor: the population of the city.
items.markingKey: B1 correlation is not causation; B1 suitable third factor. [2]

items.stem: Yusuf plots a scatter graph of the number of hours of sunshine against the number of umbrellas sold for some days. Yusuf draws the line so that all the points are above it. Explain what is wrong.

items.stem: Tariq draws a scatter graph of the midday temperature (°C) and the number of hot drinks sold for some days. The data have x-values from 5 to 30. items.answer: (a) Negative correlation (b) −3 (c) 94 (d) No: 55 is outside the range 5 to 30, so this would be extrapolation and the pattern may not continue.

items.stem: A farmer weighed 41 apples. The mass of each apple is m grams. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. items.stem: A garden centre in Kuala Lumpur records its sales, in thousands of dollars, each quarter. The data cover 2022 to 2026. Explain why a 4-point moving average, rather than a 3-point moving average, should be used to show the trend.
items.answer: There are four quarters in a year, so each 4-point moving average contains every season exactly once; this removes the seasonal variation and shows the trend.
